system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Multi-scale positional residuals
SUMMARY: Subtract positional medians computed at several grid resolutions (full grid, 2x2-pooled, 4x4-pooled) and map the combined residual through one leave-one-out support CDF, so coarse anatomy offsets and fine structure offsets are removed without estimating each from a few values.
HYPOTHESIS: Multi-scale positional residuals improve pixel AUROC by at least 0.5 points over the single-scale residual CDF on aligned held-out datasets at K <= 4, with smaller variance across support draws.
RATIONALE: The single-scale residual estimates one median per grid position, which at K = 2 is noisy. Multi-resolution decompositions (as in image pyramids and wavelets) estimate coarse components from many values and fine components from few, and combine them with shrinkage. Applying this to positional normal offsets gives a better bias-variance trade-off at small K while keeping the method inductive.
METHOD: 1) For each branch and level: medians at pooling factors {1, 2, 4} from LOO support maps; combined offset o_j = sum_s w_s med_s(j) with w_s proportional to the number of values per cell (shrinkage). 2) r = s_j - o_j; F(r) from the LOO support residual reference. 3) 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: single-scale residual CDF. Metric: mean and standard deviation of AUROC over support draws. Falsified if no gain at K <= 4 on aligned datasets.

Idea B:
TITLE: Content-conditioned expected-normal-score regression
SUMMARY: Train on the source modalities a small regressor that predicts the expected normal anomaly score of a patch from its frozen CLIP feature, and normalise target scores by the residual from this prediction (re-centred with the supports), removing anatomy-driven offsets without assuming spatial alignment.
HYPOTHESIS: Content-conditioned residual normalisation improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over global support percentiles on all six held-out datasets, including the unaligned ChestXray and HIS where positional residuals do not apply.
RATIONALE: The residual parent removes anatomy offsets by grid position, which only works where images are aligned. The underlying cause is that some normal tissue types score systematically higher; this is a property of the patch's content, not of its position. A regressor from frozen CLIP features to the score of normal patches, trained on the source modalities' normal images, predicts this offset for any patch, and the residual is then mapped through the support CDF. Because the regressor is trained on sources only and re-centred with the target supports, the method stays inductive and leave-one-modality-out.
METHOD: 1) train_offset.py (per fold): on normal source training images, collect (frozen level-l patch feature, branch score) pairs; fit a 2-layer MLP (768-128-1) per branch and level with MSE, 5 epochs. 2) Target: r = s - g(f) - c, where c is the median residual of the supports (LOO). 3) F(r) via the LOO support CDF of residuals; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: hidden size 128; ablation with a linear regressor.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: positional residual CDF; global CDF. Falsified if no gain on ChestXray and HIS over global percentiles.

WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
